acceptedAnswer.text: Retention marketing is the work of keeping the customers and enquiries you already paid for, through timely messages on WhatsApp, email and calls and through loyalty programmes, so they buy again or complete a decision.

mainEntity.name: How does retention marketing work with MMC?

acceptedAnswer.text: We start from your own data, build funnels for welcome, reorder, nurture and win-back, and measure repeat purchase or lead progress every week. We adjust the flows as the numbers come in.

A monthly scope, agreed after a call. It is written down so you can see what each month covers. We do not publish a price list, because the right scope depends on your site, your market and how much you want done.
No. We cannot guarantee a repeat rate, because it depends on the product, the price and the customer. We commit to well-built flows, clean measurement and honest reporting.

D2C brands that want more second orders, and B2B and education teams that need follow-up so enquiries do not go cold. Not only D2C. We work with D2C, B2B and education brands, and set the work up differently for each: D2C on contribution margin and repeat purchase, B2B on the cost of a qualified lead, education on enquiries, visits and admissions.

leaks.note: Screens are illustrative recreations of each platform's interface, not client data. Platform names and logos belong to their owners.
leaks.lede: Most brands spend on acquisition and stop there. Each stage below is where a customer or lead is lost, and the retention work that keeps them.

stages.breaks: Sending the same message to everyone.
stages.why: A first-time buyer, a loyal repeat customer and an enquiry that went quiet need different things. One message for all of them fits none of them.
stages.does: We group your customers and leads by what they did (bought, browsed, enquired, went quiet), so every message has a reason to be sent.

stages.why: The first weeks decide whether someone buys again. A buyer who does not know how to use a product, or a lead who hears nothing, drifts away.
stages.does: We build welcome journeys on WhatsApp and email that confirm, guide and reassure, so the first experience is a good one.

stages.why: Many enquiries are not ready on day one, in B2B and in education especially. The brand that keeps sensible contact is the one remembered.
stages.does: We build nurture funnels of WhatsApp, email and call reminders, triggered from your CRM, that keep each lead warm until they are ready.

stages.breaks: Waiting for customers to remember you.
stages.why: For products that get used up, the moment to reorder is predictable. Miss it, and the customer buys from someone else.
stages.does: We time reorder reminders and cross-sell messages to when a customer is likely to need the product again.

stages.breaks: Treating a lapsed customer as lost.
stages.why: Winning a new customer costs more than reactivating one who already knows you.
stages.does: We run win-back offers and loyalty programmes that recognise repeat customers and give lapsed ones a reason to return.

good.t: You already have customers or leads, and repeat purchase or follow-up is weaker than it should be.
good.why: Keeping a customer you paid for is cheaper than finding a new one, which helps D2C repeat rate and keeps B2B and education enquiries from going cold. For admissions, see education marketing.
